## The data-generating mechanism {#sec-dgm-overview}

Replicate 5 is one trial drawn from the report's S2 cell. Its mechanism, stated here so that the
assumptions behind the analysis are on the table before it starts, is built from ACTG 175: a Weibull
accelerated-failure-time model is fitted to the trial and expanded to a super-population of 20,000
rows by a Gaussian copula. A region of about 20% of patients is planted by a logistic model (odds
ratio 3 on symptomatic status, no CD4 term), and its baseline hazard is shifted by $r = -\log 4$.
Every patient's hazard ratio is $b = 0.55$ outside $H^*$ = {CD4 $\le$ 230} and $h = 2$ inside it
(S2's harm), **in every region**; all hazards are then multiplied by 3. A trial is $n = 1{,}000$
patients drawn from the super-population, 1:1, entry uniform over 11 months, analysed at 40 months,
with administrative censoring only. The full build, the other cells and the checks against the
committed record are in @sec-dgm onward.

## Analytic predictions before the analysis {#sec-predictions}

Before a single Cox model is fitted, the design's event probabilities can be computed with no
simulation. The report's Table 2 (the manuscript's analytic-predictions table) computes them from the
build above; a reader with one trial in hand can produce the same column from the trial itself. Three
calls do it: rebuild the mechanism **from `rep5_trial.csv`**, with its region taken as observed and
S2's stated effects ($h = 2$ in $H^*$ = {CD4 $\le$ 230}, $b = 0.55$ outside; the region's prognostic
shift $r$ is estimated from the trial); `ahr_population()` at the design's window; `ahr_design()` at
the trial size.

```{r pre-build}
#| code-fold: show
trial_pre <- rd("rep5_trial.csv")
trial_pre <- trial_pre[, setdiff(names(trial_pre), c("id", "flag_harm"))]  # a real trial has neither
names(trial_pre) <- sub("^z_", "", names(trial_pre))                       # plain names; the build adds z_
w_pre <- character(0)
t_pre <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
dgm_pre <- withCallingHandlers(
  inject_mrct_structure(
    trial_pre,
    outcome_var = "y_sim", event_var = "event_sim", treatment_var = "treat_sim",
    continuous_vars = c("age", "wtkg", "karnof", "preanti", "cd40", "cd80"),
    factor_vars = c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
    x_pred = "cd40",
    spline_spec = list(knot = 300, zeta = 800, log_hrs = rep(log(0.55), 3)),   # b = 0.55 everywhere
    region = list(observed = "region"),                                       # region as recorded; r estimated
    x3 = list(vars = "cd40", cuts = list(cd40 = 230), loghr = log(2 / 0.55)), # h = 2 in H*
    n_super = 20000, expand = "copula", seed = 7L,
    continuous_vars_cens = c("age", "cd40"), factor_vars_cens = "symptom"),
  warning = function(cnd) { w_pre <<- c(w_pre, conditionMessage(cnd)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
pop_pre <- ahr_population(dgm_pre, analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
p_pre <- ahr_design(pop_pre, b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)$prob
t_pre <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_pre
r_pre <- dgm_pre$mrct$region$prognostic_loghr
c(region_prognostic_loghr = r_pre, generating_r = -log(4),
  build_warnings = length(w_pre), seconds = round(t_pre, 1))
```

The seven analytic rows of the report's Table 2 follow from four of the design probabilities: with
$A$ = {ITT ub < 1.0}, $B$ = {region ITT > 1.0} and $C^*$ = {region($G^*$) < 1.0}, consistency is
$A \setminus B$, non-consistency (the trigger) is $A \cap B$, oracle consistency (the oracle joint)
is $A \cap B \cap C^*$, and row (7) adds the two routes to consistency. The same four quantities are
in the campaign's analytic record (`predictions_full.csv`), which gives the report's column beside
this build's.

```{r pre-table}
#| code-fold: show
pA <- p_pre[["p_itt_ub_lt1"]]; pB <- p_pre[["p_region_itt_gt1"]]
pAB <- p_pre[["p_trigger"]];   pABC <- p_pre[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]]
rows_of <- function(a, b, ab, abc) c(a, b, a - ab, ab, abc, ab - abc, (a - ab) + abc)
rows_pre <- rows_of(pA, pB, pAB, pABC)
# the report's column, from the shipped analytic record of the S2 cell
pr <- rd("predictions_full.csv"); pr <- pr[pr$cell == "S2_rmlog4" & pr$set == "", ]
pq <- function(q) { v <- pr$value[pr$quantity == q]; stopifnot(length(v) == 1); v }
rows_rep <- rows_of(pq("p_A"), pq("p_B"), pq("p_A_B"), pq("p_A_B_Cstar"))
# identities by construction, and the record column prints the report's Table 2 values
stopifnot(near(rows_pre[3] + rows_pre[4], rows_pre[1], 1e-12),
          near(rows_pre[5] + rows_pre[6], rows_pre[4], 1e-12),
          near(rows_pre[3] + rows_pre[5], rows_pre[7], 1e-12),
          identical(f3(rows_rep), c("0.844", "0.326", "0.602", "0.241", "0.187", "0.054", "0.790")))
lab <- c("(1) P(ITT ub < 1.0): the trial is positive",
         "(2) P(region ITT > 1.0)",
         "(3) P(consistency): positive, region ITT ≤ 1.0",
         "(4) P(non-consistency): the trigger",
         "(5) P(oracle consistency): the oracle joint",
         "(6) P(oracle non-consistency)",
         "(7) P(consistency or oracle consistency)")
knitr::kable(data.frame(row = lab, `this build (from rep5_trial)` = f3(rows_pre),
                        `the report (Table 2, S2)` = f3(rows_rep), check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
             caption = "Analytic predictions under S2's assumptions: computed from rep5_trial beside the report's Table 2 S2 column. Rows (8)-(9) of Table 2 are campaign-observed, not analytic (@sec-case-campaign, @sec-sims).")
```

The two columns are close and are not expected to be equal: this build starts from one simulated
trial of 1,000 patients (its covariates re-expanded by the copula) and estimates the region's
prognostic shift from it ($\hat r$ = `r f3(r_pre)`, $e^{\hat r}$ = `r f3(exp(r_pre))`, against the
generating $-\log 4$ = `r f3(-log(4))`), where the report's column comes from the build of
@sec-dgm-overview. Differences of a few hundredths are sampling, not error. Consistency,
non-consistency and oracle consistency are the manuscript's names; this article's trigger is the
non-consistency event and its oracle joint the oracle consistency, as the rows state. Any build
warnings are the censoring model's fit and are explained in @sec-own-sims. *With your trial:* the
same three calls, with your columns and your stated $H^*$, $b$ and $h$ (@sec-own-sims walks through
them); if P(non-consistency) is very small at your design, a campaign will have few triggered trials
to summarise.
